newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Mass wartime grave discovered in Vietnam.
newsitem.headline: Mass wartime grave discovered in Vietnam.

text.p: The remains of at least 30 North Vietnamese servicemen who were killed in the Tet Offensive of 1968 have been discovered in the central highlands province of Kon Tum, a local official said on Friday.
"We have found so many remains that we cannot identify anyone," said Le Thuan Hiep, an administrator at the local Labour, War Invalids and Social Affairs department.

Local residents had long known that a group of soldiers were killed and buried nearby. But the grave's exact whereabouts had remained a mystery until this week, when a family dug under their house to make a water well.
Scattered among the remains were personal effects such as water canteens, belts, rubber sandals, coins, razor blades and bullets for Chinese-made pistols.
The Tet Offensive was one of the most bloody campaigns of the Vietnam War, which ended with a communist victory over U.S.-backed South Vietnam in 1975.
More than three million Vietnamese people died in the war and some 300,000 are still counted as missing in action.
